generic.description: A typical connection in New York: the median of what people there measured, whatever their kind of access

sources.name: M-Lab NDT city statistics: median download, upload and minimum round trip to the nearest server (delay is half that round trip)
sources.citation: The M-Lab NDT Data Set, 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-26, via the M-Lab statistics service. https://www.measurementlab.net/tests/ndt/

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Jitter (30% of the access delay) and loss (0.1%): the statistics give neither.

media-private-network.description: Media-industry private network: managed studio-to-studio links, low loss, guaranteed bandwidth

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: A managed service on dedicated fibre to the provider's edge in the same metro, with a committed rate: about a millisecond, almost no variation, loss close to zero.

enterprise-fibre.description: Dedicated enterprise fibre line: symmetric, uncontended, one or two hops to a backbone

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Uncontended point-to-point fibre: light in a few tens of kilometres of fibre plus one or two routers.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Shared fibre access with a business-grade contention ratio and a symmetric plan.

consumer-fibre.description: Consumer fibre to the home: fast down, slower up

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Passive optical access shared by a few dozen homes: a few milliseconds to the first major network, little variation; a typical asymmetric plan.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: The upstream's request-and-grant scheduling adds several milliseconds and most of the variation; upload is a small share of download.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Interleaving for error correction and the copper line's length add ten milliseconds or more; rates of a typical short-loop plan.

fixed-wireless.description: Fixed wireless access: a rooftop antenna to a nearby mast

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: A shared radio channel with scheduling, more variation than a wire, and some loss in rain or interference.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Radio scheduling and the mobile core add a few tens of milliseconds and much of the variation; losses the radio's retransmissions do not hide come in short bursts, at handovers and fades.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Shorter radio slots than 4G halve the access delay; most deployments still share the 4G core, so not the single milliseconds of the standard's targets.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: Satellites some 550 km up add only a few milliseconds of light; scheduling and the path to a ground station add the rest. Each switch to another satellite, every few tens of seconds, loses a burst of packets.

sources.name: wanpire's estimate for this kind of access
sources.basis: 35,786 km up and down again is at least 239 ms each way at the speed of light; the link's scheduling and the ground station add about 50 ms.
